title: Welcome to our first annual Australian Stock Assessment Community of Practice Workshop!
text: Our Community of Practice was officially launched in April 2026, with the mission to build a collaborative community of stock assessment practitioners to better support sustainable fisheries management. You can read more about the Community of Practice in our 1-page summary.

title: Welcome to our first annual Australian Stock Assessment Community of Practice Workshop!
text:
Who is this conference for?
This workshop will comprise of two parts:

Days 1 to 2 of this workshop is generally aimed at stock assessment scientists. The schedule contains conference style activities for introduction and networking.
Days 3 to 5 is aimed at both stock assessment scientists and fishery managers. Over these three days, Prof Andre Punt will lead his course “MSE with Managers”.

If you are unsure which part is best for you, get in touch.
All 5 days of the workshop will be delivered in a hybrid format (both online and in person). Links to the Microsoft Teams meetings will be sent out a few days before the workshop.

text:
Census
Tuesday night is Census night! If you’re staying away from home on Tuesday night to attend our workshop, read up on how you should complete the census. Note the following instructions taken from the ABS website:
Staying at a hotel, motel, or other holiday accommodation (including Bed and Breakfasts)

If you’re staying in a hotel, motel or other holiday accommodation away from home, you’ll need to complete a Census form.
The accommodation staff will hand out Census forms to all guests and collect completed forms. Please check with staff if you don’t get a form.
If you prefer, you can complete the Census online wherever you can access the internet. Use the login details on the front of your paper form or you can get a Census number. You’ll need to use a mobile phone to complete the process of getting a Census number and password.

Staying in short-term accommodation (Airbnb, Stayz or a holiday rental)

You’ll need to complete a Census form wherever you are staying on Census night.
If you’re staying at short-term accommodation such as an Airbnb or Stayz, the easiest way to complete your Census is online.
You can get a Census number and complete your Census online wherever you have access to the internet. You’ll need to use a mobile phone to complete the process of getting a Census number and password.

title: MSE with Managers
text:
Andre Punt will be leading this course and Kristin Privitera-Johnson will be assisting.
Huge thanks to Brett Crisafulli for the following instructions.




To get ready for the “MSE for Managers” class, you will need to install a few programs and packages. This will ensure the interactive course materials run smoothly on your machine.
For those who are unfamiliar with this software, please do not be concerned. You will not be writing any code. You will simply be using interactive apps to explore and demonstrate some of the course concepts.
For context, here is a quick breakdown of what we will be using:

R: The underlying statistical programming language that processes the data.
RStudio: The application we use to view, organise, and interact with R.
Shiny: A tool that turns R code into user-friendly, interactive web apps.
























To get set up before the workshop, please follow the steps below.

Install the required software

Install the following two programs: R for Windows 4.6.1, and RStudio 2026.07.1
They will take about 10 minutes to complete.

Download the course materials

While the software is installing, download the course materials from the Google Drive.
Click the Download all button in the top right corner to get a ZIP file containing the Examples, Lectures, and References.

Extract the files (important)

Once downloaded, you must extract or unzip the folder to a location on your computer.
The Shiny apps will not run if they are still inside the ZIP file.

Run a test app

To make sure everything is working, open one of the four Shiny apps included in the materials:

Navigate to the extracted folder and open Examples > Example 1.
Shiny apps consist of a few different files, but you only need to open the ui.R file. Double-click it to open it in RStudio.
Once open, RStudio may show a yellow banner across the top asking you to install packages. You can ignore this banner. We are going to install the six required packages all at once.
In RStudio, look for the Console window (this is usually the bottom-left panel).
Copy the exact line of code below, paste it into that Console window, and press Enter: install.packages(c("MASS", "shiny", "markdown", "bsplus", "RTMB", "mvtnorm"))
You will see text scrolling by as the packages download. Wait until it stops and you see the > symbol appear again. This means the installation is finished.
For the best viewing experience, we want the app to open in your web browser rather than a small pop-up. Next to the Run App button (located at the top left of the script viewer pane), click the small drop-down arrow and select Run External.

Finally, click the Run App button.
The app should now fire up in a new window. Once you have made it this far, you are fully good to go for next week.
